title: Concurrency Fundamentals
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of concurrency fundamentals using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates concurrency fundamentals.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Concurrency Fundamentals** as part of **Coroutines, Asynchronous Programming, and Concurrency**. A coroutine can suspend without blocking the thread, but it still runs on threads; scope lifetime, dispatcher choice, cancellation, and shared state remain important. Use the subtopics—Concurrency Versus Parallelism, Blocking and Non-Blocking Work, Threads and Tasks—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Asynchronous code introduces lifecycle, cancellation, and shared-state concerns. Structured concurrency and explicit data flow make these concerns easier to reason about.

items.title: Concurrency Versus Parallelism
items.text: Concurrency Versus Parallelism depends on task lifetime and execution context. Keep child tasks inside an owning scope, handle cancellation cooperatively, and avoid unsynchronized shared mutable state.
